label: Delimiter step, boosted by first token l/i/h, last token v/j/t, or L=3
explanation: Fires almost only at the <DEL> step: 97% of activation mass and 94% of activations, but only on about 12% of delimiter steps. It essentially never fires in the copy phase. Outside the delimiter it fires weakly on original-phase steps 1-2 (inputs 0 or u, first occurrences only). Which delimiter steps fire depends on the sequence content. Rates are highest when the first original token (the next output) is l, i or h (4-8x lift; these carry most of the top-quartile activations), when the last original token is v, j or t, and when L is short (L=3 rate 9.6x, L=4 3.1x). The next token after that (orig(1), mainly i/h/l/r) also has some effect. The predicate combining these factors gets dev F1 0.48 / mass recall 0.77, compared with F1 0.21 / mass recall 0.97 for phase==1 alone. The remaining selectivity is a diffuse mix of token identities, so the explanation is incomplete.
